scope: Review of item-strength usage in live DK-Gen.G and BLG-JDG analysis on 2026-08-01.
finding: Item strength was not incorporated with sufficient explicitness or consistency.

whatWasMissing: which carries were ahead or behind in completed items
current one-item, two-item, and component breakpoints
frontline durability relative to enemy damage completion
whether nominal waveclear and damage were currently functional from item state
item concentration versus distributed team gold

affectedReads.assessment: The live reads relied mainly on score, gold, structures, objectives, and draft. Exact item breakpoints were not explicitly verified, so the analysis could not fully distinguish functional damage from theoretical damage or distributed gold from usable carry power.

affectedReads.event: Bilibili Gaming vs Beijing JDG Esports — Game 2
affectedReads.assessment: The kill-Over leans over-weighted engage density without checking whether current completed items supported repeated two-sided damage. The handicap reads also lacked explicit confirmation of whether BLG's growing lead was concentrated on carries capable of converting into a late kill-margin expansion.

modelImpact.reason: Active LoL procedure already requires relevant completed-item distribution and functional-damage assessment. The omission was a failure to enforce an existing gate, not merely missing optional context.

operationalRule: For every live LoL assessment at or after the first major recall cycle, record each carry's completed items and meaningful components when visible.
State whether the gold lead is concentrated on primary damage, frontline, support, or unspent gold.
Do not call damage, waveclear, frontline, or engage functional without item-readiness confirmation.
If item icons cannot be read reliably, state item strength as unknown and cap the verdict at NO BET or LEAN according to the market's existing gates.
For kill totals, compare current damage completion against frontline durability before projecting fight lethality.
For kill handicaps, evaluate whether the favorite's item distribution supports clean wipes and margin expansion rather than only map control.
decision: No new hard model version. Enforce the existing item-distribution and functional-damage requirements explicitly in every future synchronized block.
